previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation, multiple CVAs, tracheostomy, ileostomy, diabetes, and recurrent infections was admitted after a respiratory arrest due to mucus plugging. He was transferred from an outside facility where he required CPR and suctioning of a large mucus plug. CT imaging revealed multifocal lung opacities concerning for aspiration or pneumonia. He was treated with IV antibiotics for Pseudomonas and Proteus from sputum cultures and fluconazole for a yeast urinary tract infection. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. His mental status improved, and he was weaned to lower oxygen support. Repeat imaging showed resolving lung opacities. He was discharged to extended care on oral antibiotics, with instructions to continue Coumadin and monitor INR, manage pain, and care for his tracheostomy and skin.

#Urinary tract infection- In the past had been infected by 
___ which was sensitive to Cefepime. Does have 
a chronic indwelling urinary Foley which obviously puts the 
patient at risk for recurrent UTI's. Had systemic signs of 
infection given fever and leukocytosis initially. After a brief 
complication of the urinary Foley balloon inflating in the 
penile urethra presumably due to the Foley being pulled on by 
the patient, urology replaced the Foley catheter with bedside 
cystoscopy and no complications. After the Foley replacement his 
urine turned from white to yellow with no signs of pus. He grew 
Proteus from his urine and was treated with a 7 day course of 
Zosyn which ended ___. Blood cx have been negative to date. 
.
#Potential Pneumonia- The patient had a questionable opacity on 
CXR with a potential aspiration event during the ambulance ride 
to the ED. Given frothy secretions and sputum covered initially 
for anaerobic/gram positive pathogens with Tobramycin and 
Vancomycin. However given the fact he has been afebrile and 
secretions have decreased,discontinued Vancomycin and Tobramycin 
which the patient tolerated well and his initial presentation 
most likely represented a aspiration pneumonitis .Remained 
afebrile and clinically stable off pneumonia coverage. Continued 
albuterol and ipratropium nebs. He did grow  STENOTROPHOMONAS 
(XANTHOMONAS) MALTOPHILIA, SERRATIA MARCESCENS, PROTEUS 
MIRABILIS from his sputum. 
.

episodes of blood leaking from trach. site. Oxygen saturations

of previously seen right PICC line.  Midline tracheostomy tube is again seen.

The left base opacity is seen which may reflect atelectasis or aspiration
although superimposed infectious process cannot be entirely excluded.  The
right lung is clear.  No large pleural effusion or pneumothorax is seen. There
are low lung volumes.

atelectasis, although early consolidation cannot be excluded.

infiltrate.
